title: Lagoon (amusement park)
categories: Buildings and structures in Farmington, Utah
Tourist attractions in Davis County, Utah

fields.Operating season: Late March – last Sunday in October

rows: One of the oldest roller coasters in the United States. Partially damaged by fire in 1953 but repaired and reopened.
87-foot lift hill with back-to-back double loop and two large helices
A small coaster intended for young children with only a small drop and hill
The second wild mouse coaster to be located at Lagoon. Features tight turns and sudden drops.
Originally called "The Spider and the Fly". Features tight turns and spinning cars.
A Suspended Family Coaster and the only inverted coaster at Lagoon
A short family coaster with smooth turns and small drops
The second-steepest roller coaster in the United States, with a first drop at 116 degrees. It features several inversions.

Development began in 2015, and construction began in 2018, but the latter was temporarily suspended due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Construction resumed in early 2021. Primordial opened towards the end of the 2023 season. It has interactive 4D elements.
An airplane ride with vehicles looping sideways while circling a central point

Consists of 20 cars around a disc. As the ride begins to spin, the disc stays in a horizontal position. When speed and centrifugal forces increase, the ride is lifted to a near-vertical position as the disc continues to spin. [ 25 ]
Similar to a Ferris wheel, but with inverting cars
A drop tower with two different ride types: "Blast Off", a rapid vertical ascent, and "Re-Entry", a slow ascent followed by a powered drop
Six radial arms that spin as the entire ride rotates through an oval arc in either direction [ 26 ]
A river rapids ride. Features a tunnel and several waterfalls.
An airplane-type ride. Riders can move the front sail of their cars freely.
A Herschell–Spillman Company carousel built circa 1913 and installed at Lagoon in 1918. [ 27 ]: 3
A 150-foot Nauta-Bussink R50 wheel with spinning gondolas
An elevated gondola ride that spans across the entire park
A ride with a spinning platform and individually spinning cars
A train ride that goes through a tunnel and circles Lagoon Lake, passing by many animal exhibits
A spinning ride that has many near miss elements
Family ride that swings with the movement of the gondola
Small boats travel in an oval formation while surfaced on water.
Riders sit in small whale carts that jump up and down.
An airplane ride on an oval track with tight turns. The airplanes slightly tilt on the turns.
A family spinning ride with a Chinese dragon theme; rotates clockwise, then reverses direction.
Spaceship carts that move in a circular formation.
Robotic sea creatures serve as cars that travel in a circular formation. Sea creatures squirt water at riders while riders use joystick controls to avoid the water.
A spinning ride with Jeep carts.
A ride meant for small children with themed helicopter carts that can go up and down using a joystick you control.
A ride with safari jeeps that bounce while rotating in a small circle.
A small spinning ride with animals as cars.
A small airplane ride with two-person cars.
Miniature cars going around a track.

One of the first Skycoaster rides in the United States. The launch tower is 153 feet (47 m) tall and the main arch is 173 feet (53 m) tall. The flyers are raised up to a height of 143 feet (44 m). When they are instructed to do so, one of the flyers pulls the rip cord and then they drop rapidly, reaching speeds up to 80 miles per hour (130 km/h) and experiencing sensations similar to skydiving.

Go-karts attraction that consists of two separate tracks: Lightning at 1,146 feet (349 m) and Thunder at 1,142 feet (348 m). Each track has 28 cars and features several sweeping turns, overpasses, 360-degree spirals, straight-aways, and camelbacks.
Hurls two passengers at a time up to 250 feet (76 m) in the air.
Features four slides: Pipeline, Shout, Twist, and Wipeout
Features three slides: Backdoor, Ripcurl, and Seasnake
Features two slides: Liquid Lightning and The Drop
